system.name: Klotski
system.one_liner: an efficient MoE inference engine that reduces pipeline bubbles via an expert-aware multi-batch pipeline

components.name: Attention
components.role: attention sublayer within an MoE block

components.name: MoE Layer
components.role: sparse layer containing a gating network and multiple experts

components.name: Gate
components.role: gating network computing routing weights via softmax and activating top-k experts

components.name: E1
components.role: an individual expert (FFN), sparsely activated per token

components.name: E2
components.role: an individual expert (FFN), sparsely activated per token

components.name: E3
components.role: an individual expert (FFN), sparsely activated per token

components.name: E4
components.role: an individual expert (FFN), sparsely activated per token

components.name: Add & Normalize
components.role: residual add and normalization applied after attention and after the MoE layer

components.name: MoE Block
components.role: repeated transformer block combining attention and an MoE layer, stacked to form the model

components.name: Embedding Inputs
components.role: token embeddings fed into the stack of MoE Blocks

components.name: Embedding Outputs
components.role: output embeddings produced by the stack of MoE Blocks, used to predict the next token

content.key_idea: Each MoE block sparsely routes each token through a gate to a small subset of experts inside the MoE layer; during autoregressive inference this stack runs once over the whole prompt in the prefill stage and then once per generated token in the decoding stage.
content.reading_order: Left panel, bottom-to-top through one MoE Block (Attention, Add & Normalize, MoE Layer with Gate and E1-E4, Add & Normalize); right panel, left-to-right across stacked MoE Blocks for the prefill stage's full prompt, then per-token for the decoding stage.

evidence: The MoE architecture primarily consists of multiple MoE blocks, each containing an attention layer, an MoE layer
It uses a softmax function to calculate the routing weights of each expert, then activates the top-k experts
This process comprises two stages: prefill and decoding

summary: Figure 2 presents background on the standard MoE model architecture and its autoregressive inference process, which Klotski's engine serves. On the left, a single MoE Block is expanded: an Attention sublayer and an MoE Layer (a Gate plus experts E1-E4) are each followed by Add & Normalize. The Gate applies softmax to compute routing weights and activates only the top-k experts per token, whose outputs are weighted-summed as the MoE layer's output. On the right, a timeline shows how stacked MoE Blocks are invoked during inference: in the Prefill Stage the whole prompt ('Research on MLSys') is processed at once through Embedding Inputs/Outputs, activating many experts; in the Decoding Stage, tokens are generated one at a time ('is', 'interesting', ... '<EOS>'), each requiring another pass through the MoE Block stack. This figure sets up the paper's motivation: decoding-stage batches are small and expert activation varies per step, causing I/O-bound pipeline bubbles that Klotski targets.
summary_zh: 图2展示 MoE 模型的基本架构与推理过程：单个 MoE Block 由注意力层与含门控和多个专家的 MoE 层组成，门控用 softmax 激活 top-k 专家；右侧时间线显示预填充阶段一次性处理整段提示，解码阶段逐词生成，均需重复经过堆叠的 MoE Block。
